rows.grounds: one who violates the teacher's bed

items.question: What happens at death to even the gravest sinners who have received this knowledge?
premises: A person may be a liquor-drinker, thief, brahmin-killer, or violator of the teacher's bed.
Such a person is freed at the very moment of death.
Only the body-device remains behind.
items.inference: Reception of this knowledge grants liberation at death even to those guilty of the gravest transgressions, leaving only the body behind.
uncertainties: The exact referent of the liberating knowledge is carried over from the preceding verses.
items.plain_english: Even a drinker of liquor, a thief, a killer of a brahmin, or one who violates the teacher's bed is freed at the very moment of death; only the body remains.

rows.grounds: one living at the edge of the land
one who makes the place pure

items.question: Who can become a knower that purifies the land regardless of birth, age, or residence?
premises: A person may be last-born or twice-born, child, old, or youth.
A person may live at the border of the land.
Whoever among them is a knower becomes a purifier of the land.
items.inference: Knowledge, not birth, age, or location, makes a person a purifier of the land.
uncertainties: The scope of 'land' (deśa) could mean a region or the whole country.
items.plain_english: Whether last-born or twice-born, child, old, or young, even a border-dweller who is a knower becomes a purifier of the land.

items.question: Who is present on such an occasion and who should be honored first?
premises: In that place the god is present together with the goddess and attendants.
Because of this divine presence, a primary act of honor is required.
The teacher skilled in knowledge should be established as the primary object of honor.
items.inference: Since the deity is present there with his retinue, the knowledge-skilled teacher must be honored first.
uncertainties: Whether 'there' refers to the assembly, the land, or the ritual site is context-dependent.
items.plain_english: There the god is present with the goddess and attendants; therefore, one should first honor the teacher who is skilled in knowledge.

items.question: On which occasions should the worship of the teacher's form be performed according to the Yogīśvarīmata?
premises: The worship of the teacher's form should be performed.
The Yogīśvarīmata gives the rule for this worship.
It is to be performed during the thread offering, ancestor rites, and on festival days.
items.inference: According to the Yogīśvarīmata, the teacher's form-worship is prescribed for the thread offering, śrāddha, and festival days.
uncertainties: The exact ritual details of mūrtiyāga are not specified in this verse.
items.plain_english: One should perform the worship of his form; according to the Yogīśvarīmata, this is done during the thread offering, at śrāddha, and fully on festival days.

rows.grounds: at solar and lunar eclipses etc.

items.question: What additional occasions call for this form-worship beyond those already named?
premises: Solar and lunar eclipses are occasions for the rite.
Worldly festivals, celebrations, and marriages are occasions for the rite.
Sacrificial rites performed by brahmins are also occasions for the rite.
items.inference: The form-worship extends to eclipses, worldly festivals, celebrations, marriages, and brahminical sacrifices.
items.plain_english: It should also be done at solar and lunar eclipses, at worldly festivals and celebrations, at marriages and the like, and during the sacrificial rites of brahmins.

rows.grounds: for the sake of a wish

items.question: For what ritual purposes is the form-worship performed and into how many types is it divided?
premises: The form-worship is performed at initiation, consecration, and purification of observances.
It is also performed for the fulfillment of a desire.
This form-worship is of five kinds.
items.inference: The form-worship serves major ritual and personal purposes and is classified into five types.
items.plain_english: The form-worship should be performed at initiation, consecration, purification of observances, and for the sake of a desired aim; it is of five kinds.

items.question: What are the five types of form-worship and how is the single and mixed type defined?
premises: The five types are single, paired, mixed, circle-joined, and hero-mingled.
The single type is performed by teachers alone.
The mixed type is performed by teachers together with others.
items.inference: The fivefold form-worship is distinguished by the composition of its participants, beginning with teachers alone or teachers mixed with others.
uncertainties: The exact referent of 'others' in the mixed type is clarified in the next verse.
items.plain_english: The five types are the single, the paired, the mixed, the circle-joined, and the hero-mingled. The single is done by teachers alone, and the mixed is done by teachers together with others.

items.question: How is the paired form of worship constituted and subdivided?
premises: The paired worship is performed with practitioners and others together with their wives.
The paired worship is further divided into two kinds.
It may be done through union with one's wife or through union with a courtesan brought by payment.
items.inference: The paired form-worship involves male-female partnership and has two subtypes based on the female partner.
uncertainties: The ritual meaning of 'union' (saṃyoga) may range from presence to full ritual participation.
items.plain_english: The paired worship is done with practitioners and others together with their wives; it is of two kinds, either through union with one's wife or through union with a courtesan who has been brought by payment.

items.question: What gives rise to the circle-joined worship and what is its result?
premises: The circle-women and others will be explained later as fitting partners in power-union.
Union with them constitutes the circle-joined worship.
The circle-joined worship grants all fruits.
items.inference: When the appropriate power-partners are joined in the rite, the resulting circle-joined worship yields all desired results.
uncertainties: The specific identities of cakriṇī and related figures are deferred to later verses.
items.plain_english: The circle-women and other fitting partners in power-union will be explained later; worship joined with them becomes the circle-joined rite, which grants all fruits.

items.question: What defines the hero-mingled worship and how are participants arranged within it?
premises: The worship performed together with all participants is called hero-mingled.
The teacher should be placed in the middle of them.
The group of teachers forms the surrounding enclosure.
items.inference: The hero-mingled worship gathers all types together, with the teacher at the center and the teacher-group forming the first surrounding circle.
items.plain_english: The worship performed together with all is called the hero-mingled rite; the teacher should be in the center, and the group of teachers forms the surrounding circle.

rows.grounds: extending up to the samayin level

items.question: How are the outer enclosures arranged and where is the teacher placed in alternative layouts?
premises: Outside there are three enclosures extending in order up to the pledged initiates.
All participants may instead be arranged in rows.
In every arrangement the teacher remains in the middle.
items.inference: Whether arranged in concentric enclosures or in rows, the assembly is ordered hierarchically with the teacher always at the center.
uncertainties: The exact grades included between the inner group and the samayin are not named here.
items.plain_english: Outside there are three enclosures in due order, extending up to the pledged initiates; or all may be arranged in rows, but in every case the teacher is always in the middle.

items.question: How should the assembly be honored once it is arranged in the circle?
premises: The arranged assembly is to be worshiped at that time.
Worship uses the teacher's scent, incense, garland, touch, and garment.
The worship follows the order of the circle, recognizing each as that very circle.
items.inference: The ritual honors the assembly through shared substances and garments in accordance with the circle's structure.
uncertainties: The phrase 'touch-garment' (samālambhana-vāsasā) may refer to contact with or wearing of the teacher's garment.
items.plain_english: Then, following the order of the circle, one should worship with his scent, incense, garland, touch, and garment, recognizing, 'This is that very circle.'

rows.grounds: in a circle with one spoke
the rite of a single hero
in a circle with two spokes
in a circle with six spokes

items.question: How does the form of the circle determine which ritual configuration is contemplated?
premises: In a one-spoked circle one should contemplate the single-hero rite.
In a two-spoked circle one should contemplate the paired rite.
In other circles, such as a six-spoked one, one should contemplate the triad and so on.
items.inference: The number of spokes in the circle prescribes the corresponding ritual configuration to be visualized and enacted.
uncertainties: The phrase 'trikam evaṃ' is compressed and may imply a sequence of triadic groupings.
items.plain_english: In a one-spoked circle one should contemplate the single-hero rite; in a two-spoked circle the paired rite; and in others, such as a six-spoked circle, the triad and so forth.

items.question: How are larger groups of deities matched to circles with more spokes?
premises: A six-spoked circle corresponds to six yoginīs.
A seven-spoked circle corresponds to a group of seven, and an eightfold arrangement to octads.
Any other similar grouping is placed in a circle of corresponding form.
items.inference: The deity configuration must match the structural form of the circle in which it is invoked.
uncertainties: The exact parsing of 'saptāre@ṣṭāṣṭake' is compressed and may allow slight variation in grouping.
items.plain_english: One should place six yoginīs in a sixfold form, a group of seven in a seven-spoked circle, octads in an eightfold form, or any other such group in a circle of corresponding shape.

items.question: What is the proper procedure for worship and satiation using the ritual vessel?
premises: The wise practitioner should first worship the circle in a vessel filled with liquid.
The vessel must be placed on a support.
Satiation should never be performed without a support.
items.inference: Proper ritual satiation requires first worshiping the circle in a supported, liquid-filled vessel.
uncertainties: The exact nature of the liquid (ali) is not specified in this verse.
items.plain_english: Then the wise one should first worship the circle in a vessel filled with liquid, placed on a support; satiation should never be done without a support.

items.question: Why must the ritual vessel be placed on a support during satiation?
premises: Without a support there is ritual failure.
Without a support the radiant powers are not pleased.
Without a support the vessel becomes like a ghost-form, even if it contains śākta nectar and liquor.
items.inference: The support is essential because it prevents ritual collapse and ensures the offering is received by the radiant powers.
uncertainties: The term 'rays' (raśmayaḥ) may refer to deities, energies, or subtle powers.
items.plain_english: Without a support there is a lapse, the radiant powers are not pleased, and the vessel becomes like a ghost, even if it holds śākta nectar and liquor.

items.question: How should the practitioner contemplate the triad of enjoyer, power, and Śiva during the rite?
premises: The power present there is the enjoyer.
That same reality is Śambhu, the supreme lord.
The practitioner should contemplate the united triad of individual, power, and Śiva.
items.inference: The rite requires meditating on the non-difference and union of the individual, Śakti, and Śiva.
uncertainties: The grammatical gender shift between śaktiḥ and sa śambhuḥ reflects identity rather than difference.
items.plain_english: There the power is the enjoyer, and that same reality is Śambhu, the supreme lord; thus one should meditate on the united triad of the individual, power, and Śiva.

items.question: In what order and by what method should the satiation offering be carried out?
premises: Satiation should be performed for each enclosure in sequence.
The rite uses the method of reabsorption.
Afterward the practitioner should lead the process back within.
items.inference: The satiation proceeds outward through each enclosure in order and is then withdrawn inward by reabsorption.
uncertainties: What exactly is reabsorbed may refer to the invoked powers or the ritual flow.
items.plain_english: Then the satiation should be performed for each enclosure in order; by the method of reabsorption, one should then lead it back within.

items.question: What constitutes a complete circulation in the satiation rite and what is its order?
premises: The circulation continues until it reaches the teacher.
That complete movement is called the full circulation.
In that circulation the deities are satisfied first and the heroes afterward.
items.inference: A full satiation cycle moves through the assembly to the teacher, honoring deities before heroes.
items.plain_english: When the movement reaches the teacher, that is called the full circulation; in it, the deities are satisfied first and then the heroes. Such is the order.

rows.grounds: sandhi: vīraśaktiḥ + ca + iti + evam + asmad-guru-kramaḥ

items.question: What is the teacher's prescribed order for honoring the pair and what offerings follow?
premises: According to our teacher's order, the hero and the hero-power are honored in that way.
After that, various portions of food are offered.
The food portions are accompanied by meat, fish, and other items.
items.inference: The lineage order honors the hero and hero-power together, followed by diverse food offerings including meat and fish.
uncertainties: The exact ritual status of meat and fish depends on the specific tantric context.
items.plain_english: According to our teacher's order, the hero and the hero-power are honored thus; then various portions of food, together with meat, fish, and the like, are offered.

items.question: How should the best practitioner offer food, and what substitute is used if no vessel is available?
premises: The best practitioner should scatter the food offerings in front until satisfaction is complete.
If no vessel is available, a substitute must be used.
The substitute is the bhadra or the rolled shell.
items.inference: Food offerings are scattered until satiation, and in the absence of a vessel the hand-gestures bhadra or rolled shell serve as substitutes.
uncertainties: Whether bhadra and vellitā-śukti are alternatives or used together is clarified in the next verses.
items.plain_english: There the best practitioner should scatter the offerings in front until complete satisfaction; if no vessel is available, he should use the bhadra or the rolled shell.

items.question: How does the Siddhāmata define the hand-formed substitutes for a ritual vessel?
premises: According to the Siddhāmata, the wise one should form a vessel with the hands.
The bhadra is made with the right hand.
The rolled shell is the other named hand-formation.
items.inference: In the Siddhāmata, bhadra and vellitā-śukti are specific hand-formed vessels used when a physical vessel is absent.
uncertainties: The exact formation of bhadra is not fully described in this verse.
items.plain_english: According to the Siddhāmata, the wise one should make a vessel with the hands: the bhadra is formed with the right hand, and the other is called the rolled shell.

rows.grounds: on top of the left hand
the fingers of the left hand

items.question: How is the rolled-shell hand gesture formed step by step?
premises: The little finger of the right hand is placed upon the left hand.
The forefinger and thumb are joined.
The fingers of the left hand are placed below the right.
items.inference: The rolled-shell gesture is formed by interlocking the hands with specific finger placements of right over left.
uncertainties: Some fine details of finger curvature are implicit rather than explicit.
items.plain_english: One should place the little finger of the right hand upon the left, join the forefinger and thumb, and place the fingers of the left hand below the right.

rows.grounds: when the join has no gaps

items.question: What completes the rolled-shell gesture and what ritual fault can occur during drinking?
premises: When the two hands are bound without gaps, the formation is called the rolled shell.
During the time of drinking, drops may fall from that formation.
Drops that fall to the earth indicate an imperfect performance.
items.inference: The rolled-shell gesture must be tightly sealed, because any drops falling to the ground during drinking mark a ritual defect.
uncertainties: The verse states the consequence implicitly; the remedial action is not specified here.
items.plain_english: When the two hands are bound without any gap, that is called the rolled shell; but if, at the time of drinking, drops fall to the ground, the gesture has not been properly formed.
